Subject: Thanks for the demo — follow-ups on evals, schemas, and retries

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — the team appreciated the latency numbers and the live example of structured output. A few things we want to capture as we prioritize a short proof-of-concept: 

- Model fit: we need to understand which model families you recommend for transactional customer messages (short prompts, high fidelity JSON output).
- Benchmarks: can you share a concise benchmark report for 512-token median length and 3 concurrent streams?
- Prompt sets: we attached a sample prompt set we use for order confirmations (attached: finup-prompt-set.csv).
- Schema compliance: our head of ops is strict about JSON schema validation; we expect 98%+ schema conformance.
- Retries/tooling: how does Redwood recommend handling function/tool retries when downstream systems (order API) return 5xx intermittently? Any guardrail patterns?

Next steps from our side: Priya (cc) will scope a ~2-week POC and needs a proposed eval plan and a rough cost estimate. Can you put together a short post-demo action plan (recommended models, bench link, quick eval steps, owners, and a recommended retry/backoff pattern)?

Thanks —
Ethan

Hi Ethan / Priya —

Great to chat. Below is a concise action plan and our initial recommendations so Priya can kick off the POC scoping. I attached a short benchmark summary (redwood-benchmarks-q4.pdf) and a recommended JSON schema for your order-confirmation messages (schema-order-confirmation.json).

1) Recommended models (for transactional, structured JSON output):
   - redwood-alpha-mini (low-latency, high-conformance for short prompts; lowest cost)
   - redwood-alpha (higher-fidelity, better at edge-case formatting when prompts are noisy)
   - For teams doing heavy quantization/throughput: redwood-alpha-quant8 (trade-off testing recommended)

2) Benchmarks & performance links:
   - Attached: redwood-benchmarks-q4.pdf (512-token median, 3 streams, p50/p95/p99 latency, token cost estimates)
   - Live perf dashboard (link below) shows structured-output success rates across variants and sequence lengths.

3) JSON schema conformance approach (target: 98%+):
   - Eval plan: run the attached prompt-set through redwood-alpha-mini and redwood-alpha; collect structured-output conformance metrics and examples of failure modes.
   - Use Redwood Optimize recommendations: prefix caching on static confirmations and strict output parsing with schema validator on the server-side (fail fast + human-in-the-loop for <1% fall-through).

4) Tool/function-calling & retry guidance:
   - Primary pattern: synchronous call -> attempt function call -> on 5xx, perform exponential backoff with jitter (retry: 3 attempts, base backoff 250ms, max 2s).
   - For idempotent order-confirmation calls: include a request-id token generated by your service and echoed by downstream to prevent duplicate effects.
   - For non-idempotent actions: respond with structured error code and route to a dead-letter queue; allow manual reconciliation.

5) POC scope & owners (suggested):
   - Run 2,000 prompt samples through both models (Soojin / Dylan to set up eval harness)
   - Measure: schema_conformance, token_cost, p95_latency, function_call_success_rate (Karthik to instrument)
   - Deliverable: short report + sample failure cases and suggested prompt rewrites (deadline: 2 weeks)

6) Cost estimate (rough):
   - redwood-alpha-mini POC run: estimated ~ $800 for 2k prompts (with caching suggestions)
   - redwood-alpha: estimated ~ $1,600 for same run

Next steps I will take now: share the benchmark PDF and JSON schema (attached), spin up an eval harness for the sample prompt set, and schedule a 30-minute sync with Karthik to discuss tool-call semantics.

If that aligns, Priya, can you confirm kickoff and preferred time for the technical sync (we have availability Thu/Fri this week)?

Best,
Soojin Lee

Quick technical notes from my side (will join the sync):

- Schema enforcement: the eval harness should run both soft and hard validators. Soft = fuzzy matching (allow minor formatting) for insight; Hard = strict JSON Schema v7 validation for the final conformance number. We expect some tokens to contain escaped characters or extraneous whitespace — normalize before strict check.

- Tool calling: the runtime exposes metadata for each function call (call_id, latency_ms, http_status). Capture these in the eval logs so you can correlate model choices to downstream success.

- Retries: three attempts is reasonable, but tie retry budget to SLA. If downstream average latency spikes >500ms, throttle concurrent calls rather than increasing retries; retries can make downstream load worse.

- Quantization/quality regressions: if you test quantized variants (quant8), 1) run a small smoke regression suite of 200 critical prompts first, 2) check for hallucination or fields missing in JSON. If regressions >2% on critical fields, fallback to non-quantized profile automatically. Redwood runtime supports automatic fallback to a pinned non-quantized model variant on regression triggers.

I'll prepare an instrumentation checklist for the sync and a small sample script to surface schema failures.

-Karthik
